sections.h2: Where is Greer, SC, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Greer is a city in northern South Carolina that sits in two counties, Greenville and Spartanburg. It lies about 12 miles northeast of Greenville and 17 miles west of Spartanburg, at an elevation of roughly 974 feet.

The city covers 25.56 square miles, and about 2.12 of those are water. Apalache Lake, Lake Robinson and Lake Cunningham are inside or beside the city, and the South Tyger River crosses the northern part. If your house backs up to water, mention it early, because buyers and inspectors will ask about drainage.

The county line matters to a seller more than most people expect. A 2023 estimate puts about 25,587 Greer residents in Greenville County and 9,721 in Spartanburg County. Your county decides which assessor values the house, which treasurer sends the tax bill and which Register of Deeds records the deed. Public schools follow the same split: Greenville County residents are served by the Greenville County School District, and some Spartanburg County addresses fall in Spartanburg School District 5.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Greer, and why does it still shape the housing stock?
sections.html:
Greer grew up around a railroad stop. The Richmond and Danville Air Line Railway built Greer's Station on land owned by the Greer family in 1873, and the community was incorporated in 1876 as the Town of Greer's. About a century later the name changed to City of Greer.

Textile work followed the rails. The Victor, Franklin, Apalache and Greer mills made the area a manufacturing center, the first bank opened in 1900, and the Piedmont and Northern Railway added a second line in 1914. Interstate 85 and Greenville-Spartanburg International Airport both opened in the early 1960s. When textile imports hurt the mills in the 1970s, the city recruited new industry to replace them.

For a seller, that history means Greer has older mill-era streets near the old center and newer subdivisions farther out. Older homes can carry deferred repairs, and the cost of that work is a common reason owners look at an as-is sale.

Manufacturing and logistics carry the local economy, and both are tied to the same corridor along Interstate 85. Greer is home to what Wikipedia describes as the largest BMW manufacturing facility in North America, with a supplier network that adds more jobs around it.

The South Carolina Ports Authority runs Inland Port Greer, a 91 acre container hub at 100 International Commerce Blvd, reached from I-85 at exit 58. Norfolk Southern provides an overnight express shuttle between the Port of Charleston and Greer six days a week, and the port advertises 24/7 gate access. The National Weather Service office for the Upstate is also in Greer, and two hospitals, Pelham Medical Center and Greer Memorial Hospital, are in the area.

Why this matters when you sell: people move for these jobs, and people leave for them too. A job transfer with a short deadline is one of the most common reasons an owner wants a fast closing instead of a months-long listing.

sections.h2: How does Greer weather affect an older house?
sections.html:
Greer has hot, humid summers and short, mild winters, and the wear shows up in roofs, air conditioning and gutters. NOAA normals for 1991 to 2020 put the July average high at 90.3 degrees and the January average low at 32.1 degrees.

The area gets about 49.67 inches of precipitation a year and an average of 3.9 inches of snow. That is enough rain to find every weak flashing, clogged gutter and low grade near a foundation, and enough summer heat to shorten the life of an old HVAC system.

Items worth checking before you list or take an offer:

  • Roof age and missing or lifted shingles
  • Water staining in attics, crawl spaces and under windows
  • HVAC units near the end of their service life
  • Drainage around houses close to the lakes or the South Tyger River

If the home sits near water, ask the county floodplain office what the mapped zone is before you set a price.

sections.h2: What property tax issues come up when you sell a house in Greer?
sections.html:
The tax bill depends on which county the house is in, and a sale can change the assessed value. South Carolina taxes a legal residence (an owner-occupied home plus up to five acres) at a 4% assessment ratio under Section 12-43-220, while other real estate is taxed at 6%. If the owner is later found ineligible, the 6% rate applies, and a penalty of 100% of the tax paid plus 0.5% interest per month can apply.

Greenville County explains that a qualifying sale is an assessable transfer of interest. That triggers a reassessment at current market value, with an appraisal date of December 31 of the year of the sale, and it removes the 15% cap on increases for that property. Greenville County says applications for the 4% rate are due by January 15, and the statute requires a new owner to file a new application after a change in ownership.

State law sets taxes as due between September 30 and January 15. Section 12-45-180 adds a 3% penalty after January 15, another 7% after February 1, and another 5% after March 16. Greenville County also lists January 15 as the last day to appeal the previous year's values, and says tax bills are typically mailed near the end of October. For a Spartanburg County address, we could not open an official county page, so ask the Spartanburg County assessor and treasurer for their dates and appeal steps.

sections.h2: How is a deed recorded for a Greer sale?
sections.html:
A Greenville County deed is recorded with the Register of Deeds in Greenville. The office is in Suite S-2100 of Greenville County Square, 301 University Ridge, and it is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. When you record in person, the office asks you to arrive before 4:30 p.m.

The state deed recording fee is $1.85 for each $500 of value, or part of it. Of that, $1.30 is the state portion and $0.55 is the county portion under Section 12-24-90. Some transfers are exempt, including a deed given to a mortgagee in lieu of foreclosure and deeds that only confirm title already held without payment.

The Greenville office scans documents and returns the originals. Staff will not give legal advice, and they suggest talking to a legal professional before drafting a deed yourself. Spartanburg County has its own Register of Deeds, and we did not open an official page for it, so call before you plan the closing.

sections.h2: What local rules should Greer owners know about?
sections.html:
The City of Greer says all rentals inside the city must be registered and licensed according to their classification. If the house you are selling is a rental, confirm that its license is current and that the tenant situation is clear before an inspection.

The city also has a Community Standards Division, listed in the site menu as Community Compliance, which handles code enforcement. The city office is at 301 E. Poinsett Street, and the main number is (864) 848-2150. The page does not spell out what the division enforces, so ask about open violations on your address. An unresolved complaint can slow a conventional sale because lenders and buyers want a clean record.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale look like for a Greer house?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Greer skips the mortgage approval step that most often delays a closing. You request an offer, we review the house as it is, and you choose a closing date that works for you.

  • No need to clean, stage or fix the roof, HVAC or flooring first
  • Inherited, tenant-occupied, mill-era and vacant houses are all fair game
  • A deed, a title company and the county recording steps above still apply
  • You can decline the offer and owe nothing

We cannot promise a price before seeing the property, and every offer depends on condition, location and repairs.

faqs.q: How big is Greer, SC, and what counties is it in?
faqs.a: Greer covers 25.56 square miles and sits in both Greenville and Spartanburg counties. About 12 miles separate it from Greenville and about 17 miles from Spartanburg.

faqs.q: Which county do I deal with if I sell a house in Greer?
faqs.a: It depends on where the parcel is, since Greer straddles two counties. The county that holds the parcel handles the assessment, tax bill and deed recording, so check the tax notice before you start.

faqs.q: When are South Carolina property taxes due on a Greer home?
faqs.a: State law makes them due between September 30 and January 15. Penalties start the day after January 15, with 3% added, then another 7% after February 1 and 5% after March 16.

faqs.q: Does selling my Greer house raise the property tax?
faqs.a: It can for the buyer. Greenville County treats a qualifying sale as an assessable transfer that reassesses the home at current market value and ends the 15% cap, and the new owner must apply for the 4% rate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greer house with code violations or tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase a house with open issues or tenants in place, but clearing or disclosing violations and confirming the city rental license makes the closing smoother.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Greenville County?
faqs.a: The state fee is $1.85 per $500 of value, split as $1.30 state and $0.55 county, plus any office fees on the county schedule. Some transfers are exempt under Section 12-24-40.
